correctness.rationale: Exact conditional probability identity, positivity-based finite-N exponential squeeze, strict convexity, integer lattice-phase decomposition with bounded correction, density of irrational phases, and coercive support-boundary cases were independently reconstructed. Exact-rational direct enumeration confirmed finite identities, optimal allocation bounds and boundary tests; finite checks are auxiliary to the analytic proof. The claimed asymptotics require fixed positive exclusive-good-year masses.

originality.rationale: Full Snyder (2006) and ten Brink–Gremer–Kokko (2020) model/analysis inspections yield different long-run evolutionary fitness objectives; accessible Bai–Yun–Chung (1991) uses mean cost rates; Valleriani (2006) is an unresolved but specified closely relevant source. value.rationale: The natural objective is the finite-cohort probability of obtaining any recruit before rescue resources expire under common environmental seasonal shocks. The result gives a sharp robust balance independent of correlation probabilities when two exclusive good-year risks remain possible, finite-N seed-number windows, nontrivial rounding-induced accumulation constants, and a discontinuous change when one feasible ecological scenario disappears. These are structural features of a motivated conservation-planning benchmark rather than renamings of a known tabulation; biological scope and lack of empirical persistence inference are explicitly stated.
